title: Florida Prodigy Nathan Thomas Becomes World's Youngest Professor at 18, Breaking a 306-Year Record
excerpt: Guinness World Records has certified Nathan Thomas, whose family has roots in India, as the youngest male professor in history after he began teaching engineering at Miami Dade College at 18 years and 346 days old.
body:
• Nathan Thomas became the youngest male professor in recorded history at 18 years and 346 days, shattering a 306-year-old record held by Scottish mathematician Colin Maclaurin.
  • Thomas, whose mother Merlyn Rani Thomas has Indian heritage, dual-enrolled in college at age 10 and earned both a bachelor's and master's in electrical engineering by 18.
  • He is now 21, teaches online engineering courses at Miami Dade College, and is pursuing a Juris Doctor at the University of Miami School of Law.
  • The story has been widely covered by Indian media outlets including India Today, The Indian Express, and The Times of India.

Guinness World Records has officially certified Nathan Thomas, a 21-year-old Florida engineer and educator, as the youngest male professor in recorded history. Thomas accepted a teaching position at Miami Dade College in August 2023 at the age of 18 years and 346 days, breaking a record that had stood since 1717 when Scottish mathematician Colin Maclaurin became a professor at 19.

Thomas was also 16 days younger than Alia Sabur, the American materials scientist who held the record for youngest female professor after taking up a post at South Korea's Konkuk University in 2008 at the age of 18 years and 362 days. That makes Thomas the youngest professor of any gender ever documented.

From Kindergarten Prodigy to College Faculty

Thomas's academic trajectory has been extraordinary from the start. He scored perfectly on his kindergarten readiness assessment test in 2010 at Coral Park Elementary in Florida. His mother, Merlyn Rani Thomas, recalled a school counsellor urging the family to challenge him further after a standout performance at a Christmas show.

https://x.com/nypost/status/2084323644155588650

"I remember reading him books on the steps of Thomas Jefferson's home. You know, how much more perfect could it be?"

— Merlyn Rani Thomas, Nathan's mother

Rani began homeschooling Nathan shortly after, and the family travelled to more than 20 countries — including India, the United Kingdom, France, and Germany — turning the world into his classroom. Both of Thomas's parents are engineers, and he credits them with nurturing his early fascination with mathematics and structured problem-solving.

Thomas dual-enrolled at Miami Dade College when he was just 10 years old. By 14, he had transferred to Florida International University. At 18, he had completed both a Bachelor's and a Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, graduating with honours in each.

Teaching Peers His Own Age

When Thomas walked into his first class — COP 2270: C for Engineers — at Miami Dade College in August 2023, many of the students were the same age as him. He has said the dynamic does not feel unusual.

"Once you're in that setting, everyone's there for the same reason, which is to learn. Age doesn't really factor into that."

— Nathan Thomas, speaking to Guinness World Records

Manny Perez, Dean of the School of Engineering, Technology & Design at Miami Dade College, told the college's student newspaper The Reporter that Thomas is an inspiration. "I think anytime you have the opportunity to meet a person like Nathan, you realize that there is someone special — someone who can serve as an inspiration to our students," Perez said.

A Story That Resonates With the Diaspora

The achievement has been widely covered across Indian media, with India Today, The Indian Express, and The Times of India all running prominent stories. The attention reflects the Indian diaspora's deep interest in academic excellence and prodigious achievement, particularly from families with South Asian roots.

Thomas's younger brother Noah has followed a similar path, recently becoming the youngest graduate in Miami Dade College history, topping his brother's record by three months.

What's Next

Thomas is not done with school himself. He is currently pursuing a Juris Doctor at the University of Miami School of Law, with an expected graduation date of 2028, while continuing to teach online engineering courses. He plans to practice intellectual property law with a focus on STEM fields, saying the problem-solving skills from engineering translate directly into legal work.

"If someone's willing to put in the effort, that's really all that matters to me," Thomas told Guinness World Records.
